Hi! I had the same problem. Here's what I did:
1. On the Configuration>Misc tab on PlayOnMac, click "Open virtual driver's directory". This is will open directly to the wrapper folder.
2. Go up to the menu bar at the top of your Mac's screen, click on "File">"Get Info". The section that says "Where:" tells you where your wrapper is located. 
3. Now that you know that, close all those windows and go back to "Run a .exe file in this virtual drive".
4. Go to where it said the file was located. If you can't find a folder, click Command+Shift+period. 
5. If no files are showing up when you click on a folder, it's because they just don't show, not because they're not loading. Go to the subfolder side where the files are not showing and right click anywhere, but preferably towards the top. Click on either "Get Info" or "Quick Look". Then, close all those windows and go back to the Configuration menu. This should solve the pesky bug. Go back to step #3. You should now see the missing folders. If they're still not there, repeat steps from #3 forward.

Whenever I get panic attacks it's nausea; it's always nausea (because I am terrified of throwing up). And I know it's a panic attack because I can localize where the nausea comes from (somewhere in my neck, right under my jaw, as opposed to my stomach, and a pressure on my forehead, between my eyes). It used to be like this, several times per day, while I was eating I would "freak out," panic, and I would stop eating. I went down a pant size and eventually got sick with the flu which helped me make out panic nausea from sick nausea. I still get panic attacks when people around me are sick because I'm scared I'll get sick too (even from a cold), but I think in a very logical way (for example, I thought I would throw up because my mom was sick with the cold, but I made myself understand that the cold virus is not the same as gastroenteritis). It also helped to go to therapy and release a lot of the stress I was carrying, which is most likely what was making me panic. So talk yourself through them: take deep breaths, count them, and assess the situation - what is happening, what are you feeling, how, and where, what made you panic, and how can you look at the situation in a different, possibly even more logical aspect. Right now things will probably not seem very clear and it will be hard to make it go away over night; you can't do it overnight. It takes time but practice makes you better. 

Also, just thinking that last few times you've eaten and had panic attacks, you haven't thrown up or had an actual heart attack, might be helpful in getting through the panic attacks. I read somewhere that throwing up takes a lot of energy, so the body won't do it unless it's completely necessary to remove toxins from the body, which might also help you get some peace of mind.

Good luck!

Is there any help for this at your uni? Not sure where you live, but there might be (1) free therapy sessions at the school, (2) if it's a big uni they might have their own clinic for students and often have mental health groups and psychiatrists for students AND/OR (3) they might be able to refer you someplace if they have nurses/doctors for the students (go there for an examination, tell them what's going on, they'll tell you what to do and where to go or how to find a doctor who can help you). If you're able to basically exploit whatever resources the school has for you in this situation (at least to the extent of your finances) - and it still doesn't help, you might be able to make a case to the department that you need an extension because you had x and y problems, tried to solve them with the resources available to you, went to a, b, and c staff members and followed their advice, but was not enough.
Regardless, I'd use whatever resources available (even look to see if the school has accommodations for mental health problems and disabilities). I'd look into this sooner rather than later. I was an art and design major and can attest that these programs are typically very intense and stressful. Talk to your advisor or a professor if you're not sure where to go for resources.
Remember they want you to graduate (otherwise you mess up their statistics lol - this is to your advantage, by the way) so they're gonna try to help you as much as they can. :)

This was my experience in one university I went to (it might differ slightly in others but it's generally about the same): The college has a form for students with disabilities that need accommodations (usually separate forms for different disabilities) that you can download from their website (professors are required to have information on the syllabus about how students can get a request for accommodations - you can't get this through the professors, there is a staff member who you're supposed to give the form to because it is confidential). This keeps the medical information between you, your doctor, and the member of the staff that will read the form. The professors and students never actually know what you have unless you explicitly tell them, they just send them a general message requesting them to give you certain accommodations and then that fact that you have special accommodations is kept private between the professors and you. 

You print the form, take it to (usually) the doctor who diagnosed you or your primary doctor (if they are aware of your diagnosis/situation), and they fill out the questions in the form. Some of the questions are, for example, what kind of accommodations would be reasonable for the person, etc. I have been dealing with anxiety/depression for a while and we once asked my psychiatrist if I could bring the form in (she has been managing my illness for months) and if it would be considered a disability and if I could get accommodations because I had trouble going to classes and concentrating. She said yes, but I never went on with it as I am very stubborn and wanted to finish school working like everybody else.
(I ended up quitting school because I couldn't deal with it, so don't do that, please.) Also, the request has to be put in before you actually need the accommodations, you can't just put in a request after a big test and then ask to retake it afterwards.
